newsitem.title: USA: Alyeska president eyes new Alaska oil production.
newsitem.headline: Alyeska president eyes new Alaska oil production.

text.p: The trans-Alaska pipeline has embarked on a reorganization that will improve efficiency and prepare for production from new North Slope fields, the chief executive of the system's operator said Monday.
Bob Malone, president of Alyeska Pipeline Service Co., said the changes will shift workers and contractors from the Anchorage headquarters to areas where they will be closer to system operations.

The restructuring will put about 1,000 workers in Fairbanks, about 650 in Valdez, the site of the system's marine terminal, and reduce the workforce at the Anchorage headquarters by 575 to about 125, Malone told the Anchorage chamber of commerce.
The reorganization is a business decision that does not reflect dissatisfaction with Alaska's largest city, Malone said.
"It's to move our employees to the work," he said.
The reorganization, to be completed in a few years, is expected to shrink Alyeska's overall workforce to about 1,750 from 2,230.

Alyeska this summer is marking the 20th anniversary of the pipeline's startup, and Malone said expanded North Slope production has already extended the expected life of the 800-mile oil line and marine terminal.
New oil discoveries have prompted Alyeska to boost throughput projections for 2000 by 100,000 barrels a day, Malone said.
He said he is optimistic about producer plans to tap into new North Slope oil, through enchanced recovery, satellite fields and frontier areas like the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska.
"I like what I'm hearing in the oil patch," he said. "Right now we're doing our planning (assuming that) in the year 2000 we'll be moving as many barrels as we are today."
Holding pipeline throughput at 1.4 million to 1.5 million barrels a day three years from now would require production of hundreds of million barrels of new oil, he said.
But even the state of Alaska has production forecasts that range as high as 1.6 million barrels a day three years from now, he said.

Alyeska is owned by seven oil companies with interests on the North Slope. Major owners are British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon. Mobil, Unocal, Phillips Petroleum and Amerada Hess own minor shares.
